instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, Chapter VI: registration of charges (ss. 77 to 81)
applies_to: Every company creating a charge, within or outside India, on its property, assets or undertakings, tangible or otherwise, in or outside India
Charge-holders (banks, NBFCs, HFCs, debenture trustees and other secured creditors)
A company acquiring property already subject to a charge, and any modification of a registered charge (s. 79)
excluded: Charges that the Central Government prescribes, in consultation with RBI, as outside s. 77 (s. 77(1) last proviso): see the 2022 rule exempting charges created by banking companies in favour of RBI
key_concepts: Charge: an interest or lien created on the property or assets of a company or any of its undertakings or both as security, including a mortgage (s. 2(16))
Joint filing: the particulars are signed by the company and the charge-holder (s. 77(1))
Certificate of registration (Form CHG-2) and modification (CHG-3) issued by the Registrar (s. 77(2), rule 6)
Unregistered charge is not taken into account by a liquidator (under the Act or the IBC) or any other creditor (s. 77(3)); the debt itself survives (s. 77(4))
Constructive notice from the date of registration to anyone acquiring the property (s. 80)
Registrar's register of charges is the MCA portal record, open to inspection (s. 81, rule 7)
core_obligations: s. 77(1): register the particulars of the charge, signed by the company and the charge-holder, with the instrument creating it, with the Registrar within 30 days of creation (Form CHG-1, or CHG-9 for debentures)

s. 77(1) first and second provisos: for charges created on or after 02-11-2018, the Registrar may allow registration within 60 days of creation on payment of additional fees, and on a further application within a further 60 days on payment of ad valorem fees
s. 77(1) third proviso: late registration does not prejudice rights acquired in the property before the charge is actually registered

s. 78: if the company does not register within the s. 77 period, the charge-holder may apply; the Registrar gives the company 14 days' notice and then registers unless the company registers it or shows sufficient cause; the charge-holder may recover the fees from the company
s. 79: s. 77 applies to property acquired subject to a charge and to any modification of the terms, extent or operation of a registered charge
s. 85 (read with rule 10): keep the company's own register of charges (Form CHG-7) and a copy of each instrument at the registered office
timelines: 30 days from creation or modification to file CHG-1 or CHG-9 (s. 77(1), rule 3)
Up to 60 days from creation with additional fees, then a further 60 days with ad valorem fees, on application to the Registrar (s. 77(1) provisos, for charges created on or after 02-11-2018)
Registrar's notice to the company on a charge-holder's application: 14 days (s. 78)
consequences_stated: s. 77(3): an unregistered charge is ignored by the liquidator and other creditors, so the lender ranks as unsecured in liquidation or insolvency
s. 86(1): company Rs 5 lakh and every officer in default Rs 50,000 for any default under Chapter VI
s. 86(2): wilfully furnishing false or incorrect information, or knowingly suppressing material information, in a charge filing is punishable under s. 447 (fraud)
instruments.consequences_general: Companies Act, 2013: where no specific penalty is provided, the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty of Rs 10,000 and Rs 1,000 a day for a continuing contravention, up to Rs 2 lakh for the company and Rs 50,000 for an officer (s. 450). Penalties are imposed by an adjudicating officer (the Registrar) after a hearing, with an appeal to the Regional Director within 60 days; failing to comply with the order within 90 days is an offence (s. 454). One Person Companies, small companies, start-ups and producer companies pay at most half the specified penalty, up to Rs 2 lakh for the company and Rs 1 lakh for an officer (s. 446B). Offences not punishable with imprisonment only, or with imprisonment and fine, may be compounded by the NCLT or, where the maximum fine does not exceed Rs 25 lakh, by the Regional Director (s. 441). A false statement or knowing omission of a material fact in a filing is punishable under s. 447 (s. 448).

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, Chapter VI: satisfaction of charges, receivers, company's register, penalties and rectification (ss. 82 to 87)
instruments.theme: Satisfaction, receivers and rectification of charges
applies_to: Companies whose registered charges are repaid or satisfied
Charge-holders
Persons who obtain an order appointing, or themselves appoint, a receiver or manager of charged property
key_concepts: Memorandum of satisfaction entered by the Registrar (Form CHG-5)
Registrar's own entry of satisfaction or release on evidence (s. 83)
Notice of appointment and cessation of a receiver or manager (s. 84, Form CHG-6)
Company's register of charges (s. 85, Form CHG-7)
Rectification and extension of time by the Central Government (s. 87, Form CHG-8)
core_obligations: s. 82(1): intimate payment or satisfaction in full of a registered charge to the Registrar within 30 days (Form CHG-4); the Registrar may allow intimation within 300 days on payment of additional fees, on an application by the company or the charge-holder

s. 82(2): the Registrar gives the charge-holder up to 14 days to show cause; no notice is needed if the intimation is in the specified form and signed by the charge-holder; if no cause is shown, the Registrar enters a memorandum of satisfaction
s. 83: the Registrar may enter satisfaction or release on evidence even without the company's intimation, and must inform the affected parties within 30 days
s. 84: a person who obtains an order appointing, or appoints, a receiver or manager of charged property gives notice to the company and the Registrar within 30 days, and again on ceasing to act
s. 85: the register of charges and instruments are open to members and creditors free of charge, and to others for a fee

s. 87: the Central Government may, on being satisfied that the omission or misstatement was accidental, inadvertent or for other sufficient cause, or does not prejudice creditors or shareholders, extend the time for intimating satisfaction or rectify an omission or misstatement in any earlier charge filing
timelines: 30 days from payment or satisfaction to file CHG-4, extendable by the Registrar to 300 days with additional fees (s. 82(1))
Up to 14 days for the charge-holder to show cause (s. 82(2))
30 days to notify appointment of a receiver or manager (s. 84(1))
Registrar informs affected parties within 30 days of a s. 83 entry

s. 86(2): false or incorrect information, or suppression of material information, required to be registered under s. 77 attracts s. 447

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013: powers of the Board (s. 179) and restrictions needing a special resolution (s. 180)
instruments.theme: Board and shareholder approvals for borrowing and security
applies_to: The Board of every company borrowing money, issuing debentures, investing, granting loans or giving guarantees or security
Lenders taking security or relying on the company's borrowing authority
excluded: s. 180 does not apply to private companies (G.S.R. 464(E), 05-06-2015, entry 12), if the private company is not in default in filing its financial statements or annual return (para 2A, G.S.R. 583(E), 13-06-2017)
Acceptance of deposits by a banking company in the ordinary course is not 'borrowing' (s. 179(3) second proviso and s. 180(1)(c) proviso)
key_concepts: Powers exercisable only by resolution at a Board meeting: issue securities including debentures, borrow money, invest funds, grant loans or give guarantees or security (s. 179(3)(c) to (f))
Delegation of (d) to (f) to a committee of directors, the managing director, manager or principal officer, by Board resolution at a meeting (s. 179(3) first proviso)
Borrowing limit: paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium; temporary loans from the company's bankers are excluded (s. 180(1)(c))
Temporary loans: repayable on demand or within six months, such as cash credit, bill discounting and seasonal short-term loans, but not loans for capital expenditure (Explanation to s. 180(1)(c))
Sale, lease or other disposal of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking (s. 180(1)(a)), with the 20% tests for 'undertaking' and 'substantially the whole'
Remitting or giving time to repay a debt due from a director (s. 180(1)(d))
core_obligations: s. 179(3)(c) to (f): pass a Board resolution at a meeting (not by circulation) to issue debentures, borrow, invest, or grant loans, guarantees or security; the Board may delegate (d) to (f) by a resolution at a meeting on conditions it sets
s. 179(3) Explanation II: for bank facilities, the Board approves the arrangement (overdraft, cash credit or otherwise), not each day-to-day drawing

s. 180(1)(c): obtain a special resolution before borrowing if the new borrowing plus outstanding borrowings (excluding temporary loans from bankers) will exceed paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium; the resolution must state the total amount up to which the Board may borrow (s. 180(2))

s. 180(1)(a): obtain a special resolution to sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking; the resolution may set conditions on use of proceeds (s. 180(4))
s. 117(3): file the special resolutions under s. 180, and Board resolutions under s. 179(3), with the Registrar in Form MGT-14 within 30 days (subject to the exemptions in s. 117(3)(g))
timelines: MGT-14 within 30 days of passing the special resolution or the s. 179(3) Board resolution (s. 117(1))
consequences_stated: s. 180(5): a debt incurred beyond the s. 180(1)(c) limit is not valid or effectual unless the lender proves it lent in good faith without knowledge that the limit was exceeded
s. 180(3): a s. 180(1)(a) disposal does not affect the title of a good-faith buyer or lessee, or sales and leases in the ordinary course of a business of selling or leasing

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, s. 117: resolutions and agreements to be filed (Form MGT-14)
instruments.theme: Board and shareholder approvals for borrowing and security
applies_to: Companies passing special resolutions (for example under ss. 180, 185(2) or 186(3)) or Board resolutions under s. 179(3)
excluded: Board resolutions to grant loans or give guarantees or security under s. 179(3)(f) in the ordinary course of business by a banking company, or by a class of RBI-registered NBFC or NHB-registered HFC prescribed in consultation with RBI or NHB (s. 117(3)(g) second proviso, substituted w.e.f. 22-01-2021). The MCA rules in force do not yet prescribe any such NBFC or HFC class
s. 117(3)(g) does not apply to private companies, so their s. 179(3) Board resolutions need not be filed (G.S.R. 464(E), 05-06-2015, entry 8), subject to para 2A of G.S.R. 583(E)
key_concepts: Form MGT-14 with the explanatory statement under s. 102
No public inspection or copies of s. 179(3) Board resolutions under s. 399 (s. 117(3)(g) first proviso)
core_obligations: s. 117(1): file a copy of each special resolution, and each resolution under s. 179(3), with the explanatory statement if any, within 30 days of passing it

s. 117(3)(g): Board resolutions under s. 179(3) must be filed, except a s. 179(3)(f) lending, guarantee or security resolution passed in the ordinary course of business by a banking company or a prescribed class of NBFC or HFC
No one may inspect or take copies of s. 179(3) Board resolutions filed with the Registrar under s. 399 (s. 117(3)(g) first proviso)
timelines: 30 days from passing the resolution (s. 117(1))
consequences_stated: s. 117(2): company Rs 10,000 plus Rs 100 a day for a continuing failure, up to Rs 2 lakh; every officer in default (including any liquidator) Rs 10,000 plus Rs 100 a day, up to Rs 50,000

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, s. 185: loans, guarantees and security to directors and persons in whom directors are interested (as substituted from 07-05-2018)
instruments.theme: Loans, guarantees and security: sections 185 and 186
applies_to: Every company advancing a loan (including a book debt), or giving a guarantee or security for a loan, to or for a director or a person in whom a director is interested
The director or other person who receives the loan, guarantee or security (s. 185(4)(iii))
excluded: A company that, in the ordinary course of its business, provides loans or gives guarantees or security for repayment of loans and charges interest at not less than the yield of the 1, 3, 5 or 10-year Government security closest to the tenor (s. 185(3)(b)): this covers lending NBFCs and HFCs

Loans by a holding company to its wholly owned subsidiary, and guarantees or security by a holding company for loans made to its wholly owned subsidiary (s. 185(3)(c)), and guarantees or security by a holding company for loans by a bank or financial institution to any subsidiary (s. 185(3)(d)), if the subsidiary uses the loan for its principal business
Loans to a managing or whole-time director under conditions of service extended to all employees or a scheme approved by special resolution (s. 185(3)(a))

A private company in whose share capital no other body corporate has invested money, whose borrowings from banks, financial institutions or bodies corporate are below twice its paid-up share capital or Rs 50 crore (whichever is lower), and which has no subsisting default on those borrowings (G.S.R. 464(E), 05-06-2015, entry 14), provided it is not in default in filing its financial statements or annual return (para 2A inserted by G.S.R. 583(E), 13-06-2017)
key_concepts: Absolute bar (s. 185(1)): a director of the company or of its holding company, any partner or relative of such a director, and any firm in which such a director or relative is a partner
Conditional route (s. 185(2)): any person in whom a director is interested may receive a loan, guarantee or security with a special resolution, if the borrower uses it for its principal business

'Person in whom a director is interested': a private company of which the director is a director or member; a body corporate where the director (or two or more directors together) controls at least 25% of voting power; a body corporate whose Board or managers are accustomed to act on the lending company's Board or directors' instructions (Explanation to s. 185(2))
'Directly or indirectly': structures routed through others are caught
core_obligations: s. 185(1): do not lend to, or give a guarantee or security for a loan taken by, a director, a director of the holding company, their partners or relatives, or a firm in which any of them is a partner

s. 185(2)(a): for a person in whom a director is interested, pass a special resolution; the explanatory statement must give full particulars of the loan, guarantee or security, the purpose and any other relevant fact
s. 185(2)(b): the borrower must use the loan for its principal business activities
Board approval at a meeting is also needed (s. 179(3)(f)), and the s. 186 limits and conditions apply where the borrower is a body corporate or other person
timelines: MGT-14 for the special resolution within 30 days (s. 117)
consequences_stated: s. 185(4)(i): company fine Rs 5 lakh to Rs 25 lakh
s. 185(4)(ii): every officer in default imprisonment up to 6 months or fine Rs 5 lakh to Rs 25 lakh
s. 185(4)(iii): the director or other person who received the loan, guarantee or security: imprisonment up to 6 months or fine Rs 5 lakh to Rs 25 lakh, or both

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, s. 186: loans, guarantees, security and investments by a company (as amended from 07-05-2018)
instruments.theme: Loans, guarantees and security: sections 185 and 186
applies_to: Every company giving a loan to any person or body corporate, giving a guarantee or security for a loan to any body corporate or person, or acquiring securities of another body corporate
excluded: Everything except s. 186(1) (layers of investment companies) does not apply to loans, guarantees, security or investments by a banking company, insurance company or housing finance company in the ordinary course of business, or by a company established with the object of and engaged in financing industrial enterprises or providing infrastructural facilities (s. 186(11)(a))

For s. 186(11)(a), 'business of financing industrial enterprises' includes, for an RBI-registered NBFC, giving any loan to a person or providing any guarantee or security for a loan availed by any person in the ordinary course of its business, and, for an IFSCA-registered finance company, its lending activities under the IFSCA (Finance Company) Regulations, 2021 (rule 11(2) of the Board meetings rules, as substituted on 03-11-2025)

Investments by an investment company, investments in rights or s. 62(1)(a) shares, and investments or lending by an RBI-registered NBFC whose principal business is acquisition of securities (s. 186(11)(b))
Loans to employees are outside 'person' for the s. 186(2) limit (Explanation to s. 186(2))

Loans, guarantees or security to a wholly owned subsidiary or joint venture, and acquisition of a wholly owned subsidiary's securities, do not need the s. 186(3) special resolution, but must be disclosed (s. 186(3) provisos)
key_concepts: Limit: 60% of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, or 100% of free reserves and securities premium, whichever is more (s. 186(2))
Special resolution in general meeting beforehand if the aggregate will exceed the limit (s. 186(3))
Unanimous Board approval: resolution at a meeting with the consent of all directors present (s. 186(5))
Prior approval of a public financial institution where a term loan is subsisting, unless within the limit and with no default to it (s. 186(5) proviso)
Minimum interest: not below the prevailing yield of the 1, 3, 5 or 10-year Government security closest to the tenor (s. 186(7))
Bar while any deposit repayment or interest default subsists (s. 186(8))
Not more than two layers of investment companies, subject to exceptions (s. 186(1) and the layers rules)
core_obligations: s. 186(2) and (3): keep loans, guarantees, security and investments within the limit, or obtain a special resolution in advance (except for wholly owned subsidiaries and joint ventures)
s. 186(5): pass the Board resolution at a meeting with the consent of all directors present, and obtain the PFI's prior approval where required
s. 186(7): charge interest of at least the comparable Government security yield on any loan given
s. 186(8): give no loan, guarantee or security and make no acquisition while a default in repaying deposits or interest subsists
s. 186(4): disclose full particulars and the purpose in the financial statements
s. 186(9) and (10): keep a register of loans, guarantees, security and acquisitions at the registered office (Form MBP-2 under the Board meetings rules), open to members
timelines: MGT-14 for any s. 186(3) special resolution within 30 days (s. 117)
consequences_stated: s. 186(13): company fine Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh; every officer in default imprisonment up to 2 years and fine Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh

instruments.short_name: Key definitions and power to exempt (ss. 2, 462)
instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013: definitions used in lending transactions (s. 2) and the power to exempt classes of companies (s. 462)
applies_to: Every company and every person dealing with a company in a loan, guarantee, security or charge
key_concepts: Charge: an interest or lien created on the property or assets of a company or any of its undertakings or both as security, and includes a mortgage (s. 2(16))

Free reserves: reserves available for distribution as dividend as per the latest audited balance sheet, excluding unrealised or notional gains, revaluation, and fair-value changes recognised in equity (s. 2(43))

Related party: includes a director or KMP or their relative, a firm in which a director, manager or relative is a partner, a private company in which a director, manager or relative is a member or director, a public company in which a director or manager is a director and holds with relatives more than 2% of paid-up capital, and holding, subsidiary and associate companies (s. 2(76))
Relative: members of a Hindu Undivided Family, spouses, and persons related as prescribed (s. 2(77) read with the definitions rules)

Small company: a company other than a public company whose paid-up capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore and turnover does not exceed Rs 100 crore (s. 2(85) read with rule 2(1)(t), as substituted on 01-12-2025); a holding or subsidiary company, a Section 8 company and a company governed by a special Act cannot be a small company

s. 462: the Central Government may direct that any provision of the Act does not apply, or applies with exceptions, modifications or adaptations, to a class of companies; the exemption notifications for private, Government, Section 8, Nidhi and IFSC companies are made under it
core_obligations: Read the s. 185, 186 and 180 limits with these definitions: free reserves and securities premium set the s. 180(1)(c) borrowing limit and the s. 186(2) lending limit
Check whether a s. 462 exemption notification modifies a section before relying on it for a private, Government or IFSC company

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013, s. 188: related party transactions
applies_to: Companies entering into contracts or arrangements with a related party for sale, purchase or supply of goods, property transactions, leasing, services, appointment of agents, office or place of profit, or underwriting (s. 188(1)(a) to (g))
excluded: Transactions in the ordinary course of business on an arm's length basis (s. 188(1) proviso)
Loans, guarantees and security to related parties are governed by ss. 185 and 186 rather than the s. 188(1) list
Transactions between a holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary whose accounts are consolidated and placed before the shareholders (s. 188(1) proviso, inserted in 2015)
key_concepts: Board consent by resolution at a meeting (s. 188(1))

Prior shareholder resolution where the rule 15(3) thresholds are crossed, for example sale, purchase or supply of goods amounting to 10% or more of turnover, or property transactions amounting to 10% or more of net worth
A member who is a related party cannot vote on the resolution approving that transaction (s. 188(1) second proviso)
Audit Committee approval and omnibus approval under s. 177 and rule 6A, for companies that must have an Audit Committee
core_obligations: Obtain Board consent at a meeting; interested directors stay out of the discussion (rule 15(2))
Obtain prior approval of the company by resolution where the rule 15(3) thresholds apply
Disclose the contracts or arrangements in the Board's report with justification (s. 188(2)) and record them in the register under s. 189 (Form MBP-4)
consequences_stated: s. 188(3): a contract entered into without the required consent and not ratified within three months is voidable at the option of the Board or the shareholders; a director who authorised it indemnifies the company for any loss
s. 188(5): any director or employee who entered into or authorised the contract in contravention: for a listed company, penalty Rs 25 lakh; for any other company, penalty Rs 5 lakh

instruments.title: Companies Act, 2013: private placement (s. 42), debentures (s. 71) and acceptance of deposits (ss. 73 to 76)
applies_to: Companies raising money through debentures or private placement, and companies receiving loans or other money that could be a 'deposit'
Debenture trustees and debenture holders
excluded: The deposit rules do not apply to banking companies, RBI-registered NBFCs, NHB-registered HFCs and companies specified under the s. 73(1) proviso (rule 1(3) of the deposit rules)

Many receipts are not 'deposits', including loans from banks, public financial institutions, insurance companies and scheduled banks, amounts received from any other company, amounts from a director (and, for a private company, a director's relative) who declares the money is not borrowed, secured or compulsorily convertible bonds and debentures within the limits stated, and promoter loans brought in at a lender's stipulation (rule 2(1)(c) of the deposit rules)
key_concepts: Secured debentures: charge on the company's (or its holding, subsidiary or associate company's) assets sufficient to cover principal and interest; debenture trustee appointed before the offer, and a debenture trust deed executed within 60 days of allotment (s. 71 and rule 18 of the share capital and debentures rules)

Debenture redemption reserve: not required for RBI-registered NBFCs and NHB-registered HFCs on privately placed debentures, or for listed companies; 10% for other unlisted companies, plus a 15% investment or deposit of debentures maturing in the next year where rule 18(7) requires it
